nodes.label: Isolated PDF.js viewer theming via CMD_SET_THEME and --lyceum-* variables
nodes.norm_label: isolated pdf.js viewer theming via cmd_set_theme and --lyceum-* variables
nodes.rationale: The viewer runs in its own document/origin and does not inherit parent CSS variables, so the host must post resolved token values over the versioned bridge instead of styling the host element.

nodes.label: Theme runtime flow (pre-paint -> boot.ts -> AppSettingsProvider)
nodes.rationale: React never rewrites class names on theme change; only CSS custom properties on <html> change, so the themed surface is independent of the component tree.

nodes.label: Token source of truth (palettes.ts, tokens.ts, appearance.ts, boot.ts)
nodes.norm_label: token source of truth (palettes.ts, tokens.ts, appearance.ts, boot.ts)
nodes.rationale: The catalog is defined once in TypeScript; the CSS layer maps names to runtime variables and must not define a second set of color values.

nodes.label: check-design-tokens.mjs static token checker
nodes.rationale: Guards token completeness, mapping, pre-paint fallback drift, generated PDF core currency, and keeps the legacy remap from growing.

nodes.label: Tailwind v4 @theme inline token mapping
nodes.rationale: @theme inline makes generated utilities reference the runtime variables directly, avoiding a duplicated palette in CSS.

nodes.label: Pre-paint inline theme resolution script (index.html)
nodes.rationale: Minimal pre-paint theme resolution avoids a dark flash for light users before the deferred module graph runs; palette values are deliberately not duplicated here.

nodes.label: React root mount with boot.ts before main.tsx
nodes.norm_label: react root mount with boot.ts before main.tsx

nodes.label: Smart Reader with persistent tabs and position restore
nodes.norm_label: smart reader with persistent tabs and position restore

nodes.label: EPUB content theme independence (light/dark/sepia)
nodes.rationale: Chapter content renders in its own document and cannot inherit host variables; keeping it independent from the app accent preserves a consistent reading surface, at the cost of not following accent changes.

nodes.label: Bounded legacy zinc/green compatibility remap region
nodes.norm_label: bounded legacy zinc/green compatibility remap region
nodes.rationale: It is an explicitly temporary bridge so unmigrated components still follow theme changes; it must only shrink, must receive no new selectors, and is enforced by the static checker.

nodes.label: Semantic design tokens (role-based color contract)
nodes.rationale: The previous class names mixed appearance (zinc-*), accent (green-*) and meaning; semantic tokens make palettes primitives and tokens the public contract so adding a theme or accent is not a search-and-replace exercise and light mode no longer needs a large !important remap.

nodes.label: Preload context bridge (window.api)
nodes.rationale: Renderer must not touch Node APIs directly; every native capability is exposed through the single contextBridge contract.

nodes.label: Architecture dependency check (no page imports in features, no duplicate IPC)
nodes.norm_label: architecture dependency check (no page imports in features, no duplicate ipc)

nodes.label: Runtime shape: renderer -> preload -> main -> SQLite/filesystem
nodes.norm_label: runtime shape: renderer -> preload -> main -> sqlite/filesystem

nodes.label: FOUC prevention at HTML, boot module and Electron window levels
nodes.norm_label: fouc prevention at html, boot module and electron window levels
nodes.rationale: The main process only knows the OS appearance, not the renderer's stored explicit preference, so the pre-paint script closes that gap for the page itself.

nodes.label: ADR 001: Modular monolith with explicit ports
nodes.norm_label: adr 001: modular monolith with explicit ports
nodes.rationale: Historical entry points accumulated business rules and infrastructure concerns so a small feature required coordinated edits across unrelated files; a modular monolith with explicit ports keeps one deployable product while restoring dependency direction.

nodes.label: Ports-and-adapters dependency direction (UI/IPC -> application -> domain <- infrastructure)
nodes.norm_label: ports-and-adapters dependency direction (ui/ipc -> application -> domain <- infrastructure)
nodes.rationale: Domain behavior must be reusable by desktop and mobile and native/cloud integrations must be replaceable in tests, so adapters implement core ports instead of the domain importing infrastructure.

nodes.label: Vertical-slice migration of existing code
nodes.rationale: Moving files without first separating responsibilities is intentionally avoided, so each slice migrates behavior with temporary compatibility adapters rather than a risky bulk move.

nodes.label: SQLite document-query adapter (filtering, FTS, sorting, pagination)
nodes.norm_label: sqlite document-query adapter (filtering, fts, sorting, pagination)

nodes.label: SQLite schema startup sequence (bootstrap to post-migration)
nodes.norm_label: sqlite schema startup sequence (bootstrap to post-migration)
nodes.rationale: The fixed order — bootstrap schema, bootstrap migration, application schema, versioned migrations, post-migration schema — must remain stable for existing installations and is covered by an in-memory database test.

nodes.label: Fingerprint-keyed local PDF bookmarks
nodes.rationale: Bookmarks are stored locally by PDF fingerprint with a versioned key and are deliberately excluded from cloud sync and backup.

nodes.label: Document sync flow (move/copy into managed library, mark synced)
nodes.norm_label: document sync flow (move/copy into managed library, mark synced)

nodes.label: Local SQLite data model (documents, paths, reader state, habits, word indexes)
nodes.norm_label: local sqlite data model (documents, paths, reader state, habits, word indexes)

nodes.label: Library workspace (folders, collections, cover grid, metadata)
nodes.norm_label: library workspace (folders, collections, cover grid, metadata)

nodes.label: Filesystem safety rules for library operations
nodes.norm_label: filesystem safety rules for library operations
nodes.rationale: Targets must resolve under the managed library root and unsafe paths must be rejected so a sync operation cannot escape the library or silently overwrite user files.

nodes.label: Reading entry flow (renderer -> Supabase -> cache invalidation)
nodes.norm_label: reading entry flow (renderer -> supabase -> cache invalidation)

nodes.norm_label: supabase account and shared data store

nodes.label: Cross-app file drag, copy and cut for book files
nodes.norm_label: cross-app file drag, copy and cut for book files
nodes.rationale: Users expect to drag books into WhatsApp or the desktop and to use Ctrl+C/Ctrl+X like a file manager, both inside and outside the app.

nodes.label: Sidebar keyboard hotkeys (Esc focus, Up/Down, 1-7 routes)
nodes.norm_label: sidebar keyboard hotkeys (esc focus, up/down, 1-7 routes)
nodes.rationale: Hotkey order must follow the natural route order when routes are toggled, but must never overwrite a user's manual hotkey customization.

nodes.label: Custom zoom-aware PDF text selection
nodes.rationale: Existing selection breaks on zoom; a custom selection is required because the selection layer will be changed often, using PDF.js selection only as inspiration rather than deleting it.

nodes.label: Periodic selective backups instead of per-launch backups
nodes.norm_label: periodic selective backups instead of per-launch backups
nodes.rationale: Backing up everything on every launch was excessive; periodic backups should be minimal and roughly weekly, with a settings tab for manual backups.

nodes.label: Local format conversion pipeline (src/lib/lyceum)
nodes.rationale: Conversion is done locally so users do not need Calibre, Pandoc, Kindle Comic Converter, Acrobat or kindlegen installed.

nodes.label: Built-in dictionary subsystem (manager, storage, lemmatizer, lookup)
nodes.norm_label: built-in dictionary subsystem (manager, storage, lemmatizer, lookup)

nodes.norm_label: built-in offline dictionary and vocabulary extraction

nodes.label: Lyceum (cross-platform ebook manager and reader)
nodes.rationale: One place to collect, read, understand, convert and move books without bouncing between a file manager, conversion app, reader and e-reader transfer tool.

nodes.label: Reader State Keyed by File Hash
nodes.norm_label: reader state keyed by file hash

nodes.label: Two-job render limit with 32-entry bitmap cache
nodes.norm_label: two-job render limit with 32-entry bitmap cache
nodes.rationale: Previews reuse independent canvases and a bounded cache so no second document or full-book rasterization is needed.

nodes.label: BookEdge spatial page edge in the desktop PDF reader
nodes.norm_label: bookedge spatial page edge in the desktop pdf reader
nodes.rationale: The notch shows position, not a claim that every earlier page was read; the edge is derived from the PDF outline so chapter boundaries and lengths match real page spans.

nodes.label: Riffle preview modal (6/8/12 pages, Close Look)
nodes.norm_label: riffle preview modal (6/8/12 pages, close look)
nodes.rationale: Only 'Abrir esta página' changes the reader; Escape/'Voltar à leitura' cancel without touching page, scroll offset or zoom, and focus is trapped and restored.

nodes.label: Contextual + Concept button on text selection
nodes.norm_label: contextual + concept button on text selection
nodes.rationale: The always-visible Concept button disturbs reading; it should appear only on right-click or on selection release, alongside a copy action, as an icon rather than a text button.

nodes.label: Unified GitHub Actions release pipeline (main.yml)
nodes.rationale: Only publish-release holds contents:write so platform builds cannot create independent releases; this keeps one checksummed, validated asset set per tag.
